plain: To put down a revolt or disturbance by force

webster.text: To crush; to subdue; to cause to cease; as, to quell an insurrection or sedition.

more.text: To quiet; to allay; to reduce to peace; as, to quell the tumult of the soul.

example.quote: The honorable gentleman, from his knowledge, was called upon to show the instances, and he told us the militia may be called out to quell riots.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 16, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
